LESSON: READING ALOUD

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: READING Theme 2. Family Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested L
Topic 2.4: Reading aloud
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading aloud, part of READING Theme 2. Family Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested L in Grade 5 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: Why is reading aloud important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read texts aloud on moments of the day (Morgen, Tag, Nacht),

2. read aloud texts on activities done at different moments of the day in turns,

3. read aloud texts on days of the week and match to the appropriate pictures with peers,

4. read short texts aloud and organise them in a logical order with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read texts aloud on moments of the day (Morgen, Tag, Nacht),
2. read aloud texts on activities done at different moments of the day in turns,
3. read aloud texts on days of the week and match to the appropriate pictures with peers,
4. read short texts aloud and organise them in a logical order with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading aloud together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: The learner enhances their teamwork skills as they read short texts aloud and organise

them in a logical order with peers.

Values:
Unity: Learner works collaboratively as they read short texts aloud and organise them in a logical order with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Clubs and societies: The learner explores their knowledge of club and societies as they read aloud texts on activities done at

different moments of the day in turns.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner links the concept of moments of the day to the concept of adverbs of time in English and Kiswahili.
